A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same local routing consistency study. Their complete text, equations, eight tables, 18 figures and appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite pagination and formatting changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original measurements across 20 MoE models, experiments on pretrained toy models, cache simulations, confidence intervals and offloading throughput measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the model comparisons in Tables 1–4, statistical results in Appendix E and throughput measurements in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The SRP segment estimators, SCH oracle cache using future activation frequencies, and toy-model variants are unchanged. Sections 2–3 and Appendix D describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both retain seven RedPajama domains, LMArena, OpenMath, OpenCode and OpenScience, together with the same OLMoE pretraining data for toy models. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains LRU, LFU and Fixed; Table 4 retains LRU and LFU comparisons with SCH normalized to the clairvoyant optimum. The REAL and TOY model comparison sets also match.

E3.justification: The 22,528 inputs of 512 tokens, preprocessing, model configurations, toy-model training budgets, segment lengths and cache-ratio evaluations remain unchanged in Section 3.1 and Appendix D.

E4.justification: Both retain the architecture and load-balance ablations, post-training comparisons, positional and domain analyses, layer- and expert-level analyses, and throughput case study. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix E.5 retains 95% SCH confidence intervals obtained through 1,000 bootstrap resamples. The deterministic-experiment statement is unchanged, with no new seed or repeated-run information.

E6.justification: Matched tables, figures and Appendix F report the same numerical and qualitative results. For example, Table 4 at cache ratio 2.0 still reports LRU 67.04, LFU 70.87 and SCH 90.55 relative to an optimal hit rate of 100.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 2 and Appendix C, both SRP proofs, and the throughput assumptions and reasoning in Appendix F are retained without substantive revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: two consistency metrics, analysis of 20 MoE models, load-balance and specialization findings, and the recommendation of cache sizes around twice the active experts.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning load balance, shared experts, expert combination space and domain specialization are unchanged. Appendix F retains the qualification that routing consistency alone cannot determine system throughput.

D1.justification: The new acknowledgements identify Fudan University's CFFF platform as partially supporting computational resources. This is a limited resource disclosure; Appendix D's implementation settings and the code/data release information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Appendix B are retained. Changes such as Skliar et al. from 2024 to 2025 and the Liu et al. survey from 2024 to 2026 update publication metadata for the same works.

P1.justification: v4 adds acknowledgements, corresponding-author designations and Zhongyu Wei's Shanghai Innovation Institute affiliation, and refreshes bibliographic metadata. The substantive prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adopts an ICLR conference header and different title/heading typography, with corresponding text and float reflow. Figures 11, 14 and 18 move to later pages, but all figures and tables retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: Methods, evidence, proofs and substantive discussion are unchanged. Updated references and acknowledgements provide small documentation benefits, while reflow interrupts Appendix F, previously contiguous on v3 page 28, across v4 pages 26–29. These limited editorial tradeoffs do not establish a meaningful net change in overall quality.
